findings.title: Targets are interpolated here and again inside runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates each target with applyTemplateVariables at line 52, then later calls runSplitQuery for each shard cycle (line 163). runSplitQuery now also unconditionally interpolates its targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). This repeats template interpolation for the same queries many times in the shard-splitting path. That adds avoidable work and assumes applyTemplateVariables is idempotent; repeated interpolation can also change queries if substituted values contain template-like syntax. Consider interpolating once and skipping interpolation in runSplitQuery when called from shard splitting.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are not filtered out
findings.body: runSplitQuery filters targets with `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before calling applyTemplateVariables. If a query expression is a template variable that interpolates to an empty string, the empty expression remains after interpolation and is still partitioned/grouped and passed to datasource.runQuery. This can send invalid empty Loki queries. A filter should be applied after interpolation to drop targets whose interpolated expr is empty.

findings.title: Empty interpolated expressions are no longer filtered before sharding
findings.body: The previous code interpolated queries before filtering out empty expressions. The new code filters `query.expr` before interpolation, so a target whose raw expr is a variable that resolves to an empty string is kept and passed into the shard-splitting pipeline. This can cause unnecessary shard-label lookups for an empty selector and can produce subrequests with no valid targets; runSplitGroupedQueries assumes at least one request and can fail when given an empty request list. Filter after interpolation here as well.
